_doc: THE CLONE MANIFEST of the generic `test` TLD (generic-`test`-TLD migration phase 2, 2026-08-19). It names the install ontology tipos a test needs STRUCTURE for (`roots`), the expansion policy that turns them into a closure, the `test*` TLD each cloned thesaurus becomes, and the tokens that are provably NOT clonable references (`exclude`). `scripts/clone_into_test_tld.ts` reads it, computes the closure over the repo-vendored ontology sources, allocates target tipos through `src/core/test_data/test_tld_tipo_map.json` and emits `src/core/test_data/test_tld_ontology.json`. The script REFUSES any unresolvable reference that is not listed in `exclude` — nothing is ever dropped silently. PHASE 2b (2026-08-19) adds `synthetic_thesauri`: the sections a gate addresses that have NO local ontology source at all — on the install every one of them is a clone of the seed's `hierarchy20`, so the script twins that subtree into a `test*` TLD of its own instead of dropping the reference.
_roots_doc: The PRUNED root set measured in phase 0 (scratchpad/p0/closure4.json): a tipo is a root when a fixture RQO addresses it or a non-PURE test binds it in code. PURE-token roots (the tipo is an opaque string the test never resolves) and fixture-BODY-only tipos are deliberately absent — phase 6 renames those to `test` tokens instead of cloning structure for them. The frozen foreign references of the 217 legacy `test` nodes (src/core/test_data/test_tld_foreign_refs.json) are roots too: a reference can only be retargeted at a clone that exists.

policy.size_cap: NONE (user, 2026-08-19). The closure is not truncated, no foreign-TLD stop rule, no stubbed nodes: a cloned node is a full copy of its source.
policy.parent_chain: Every cloned node keeps a real parent. A component walks up to its SECTION, which is cloned too. A cloned SECTION is re-parented (see `section_parent`) — the install `area`/grouper nodes above it are NOT cloned.
policy.section_parent: A cloned section hangs off `test1` (the shipped Test area) unless its source parent is itself in an allowed TLD (then it is kept verbatim, e.g. `es1` under `hierarchy121`), or unless the section is a thesaurus anchor, which hangs off its own `<tld>0`.
policy.subtree: The whole subtree of every cloned node is cloned (children, recursively).
policy.relations: ALWAYS followed, for every node — a relation is structure, not configuration. A cloned SECTION additionally gets `{tipo:"test24"}` (the matrix_table node whose term is `matrix_test`) and loses any source matrix_table relation, so every test record lands in `matrix_test`; a relation naming another section (a VIRTUAL section) is kept and mapped, so virtuality survives.
policy._properties_doc: Which `properties` paths make a tipo token a REFERENCE that must be cloned. A token outside these paths is still REWRITTEN when its target happens to be in the clone set — the paths only decide what the closure PULLS IN. The blocked paths are payload, not structure (default values, import column maps, tool file lists, drag targets, widget inputs, the diffusion graph).
policy._properties_strip_doc: Which `properties` paths are REMOVED from a clone outright — capability the test ontology must not own, as opposed to `properties_block_paths`, which only stops the closure from PULLING a reference in. `api_config` is the external subsystem's ONE outbound door (engineering/EXTERNAL_SPEC.md): cloning it verbatim gave the suite database a live third-party endpoint (https://zenon.dainst.org) and turned a credless unit gate into an outbound HTTP call. A cloned external section therefore keeps its shape (`search_engine`, its ddos, its fields map) and loses its endpoint, so the engine resolves it to the `external.bad_config` envelope instead of dialling out. A gate that needs a WORKING external service stubs the adapter, which is what every external gate already does.
policy._no_expand_models_doc: A node of one of these models is CLONED IN FULL but its subtree and its `properties` references are not followed: they are the diffusion/RDF projection graph, which phase 2 does not migrate. Its `relations` and its parent chain ARE followed, so the node is never left dangling.
policy.propiedades: DROPPED on clones (`propiedades: null`). It is the v5 legacy blob: the TS engine never reads it, and its free-text tipo tokens would otherwise be install references the law forbids. The 217 legacy `test` nodes keep theirs (their tokens are rewritten in place).
policy.tld_main_nodes: A `<tld>0` node is never cloned — it is a TLD main, minted by `rebuildOntology` from the `matrix_ontology_main` registry row. A reference to one is rewritten to the target TLD’s own main.
policy.require_model: A source node whose `model` does not resolve (its `ontology6` points outside the `dd` model ontology — the tch→crm CIDOC corner) is PRUNED with its subtree, and every reference to it is dropped with that reason. The engine cannot dispatch a model-less node, so cloning one would only produce a node the gate rejects. The report lists each one.
policy.band: Allocated tipos start at 1000 in every target TLD (`test1000+`); ids below 1000 are hand-authored — the 217 legacy `test` nodes and the `<tld>0`/`<tld>1` anchors a thesaurus TLD declares below.

thesaurus_tlds._doc: One `test*` TLD per cloned thesaurus (plan decision 1, user 2026-08-19): a thesaurus is provisioned, inspected and torn down BY TLD (`rebuildHierarchy(tld)` deletes a whole TLD, provisioning refuses a second hierarchy in one TLD — phase 0 §1.5), so two thesauri cannot both live in `test`. The source section becomes `<tld>1`, the terms section of the new TLD; its subtree is allocated in the same TLD from 1000. Names are STABLE — renaming one rewrites every tipo below it.

synthetic_thesauri._doc: SYNTHETIC thesaurus TLDs (phase 2b, 2026-08-19). These sections have NO local ontology source — no dd_ontology dump, no per-TLD record dump — yet a gate addresses them (as a hierarchy root, as a portal/sqo target, or with records the frozen store reveals). On the install every one of them is a CLONE OF `hierarchy20` (the seed's own Thesaurus section): a terms section whose components are hierarchy20's — the term `hierarchy25`, the `hierarchy36`/`hierarchy49` parent/children pair, the `hierarchy40` indexations, the `hierarchy93` library autocomplete. So the twin is SYNTHESISED rather than invented: `scripts/clone_into_test_tld.ts --synthetic` reads the real `hierarchy20` subtree out of the seed and clones it, whole, into a `test*` TLD of its own — `<tld>0` main, `<tld>1` terms section carrying `relations:[{tipo:"test24"}]` (matrix_test), and one clone per hierarchy20 node below it. The map keys those clones as `<source section>@<hierarchy tipo>` (the same hierarchy20 node becomes a different component in every synthetic TLD, so a plain source→target key could not hold them). `term` is a READABLE name; the identity that matters is `source_tipo` + the map key.

exclude._doc: Tokens that LOOK like a tipo but are not a clonable reference. `keep_token` leaves the token verbatim (it is not a tipo at all — it must then be registered in src/core/test_data/test_tld_foreign_refs.json with the same reason). `drop_ref` removes the innermost array element that carries it (a value in `sqo.section_tipo[].value[]`, a `ddo_map[]` entry, a `relations[]` entry). `not_a_root` only keeps it out of the root set — it is a tipo that deliberately does not exist. Anything unresolvable and NOT listed here makes the clone script REFUSE.
